name: Squirrel Bait
label: Homestead
lede: Five Louisville high schoolers, roughly two dozen shows, one LP, and a family tree that runs through Slint, Bastro and Gastr del Sol.

eras.title: Halloween in Louisville
eras.text: Two high school friends start a hardcore trio, then swap drummers and add a singer and a second guitarist until it stops sounding like hardcore.

years.src: Wikipedia: Squirrel Bait · Wikipedia: David Grubbs
years.h: Squirrelbait Youth plays its first Halloween
years.p: [[David Grubbs|f72e65e9-3ee7-4dce-9c53-5dc6221f6cd3]] on guitar and vocals, Clark Johnson on bass and Rich Schuler on drums start a hardcore trio in Louisville. A demo tape under the name follows the same year.
years.xp: Grubbs and Johnson were high school friends, and the band began as a fast hardcore trio. Grubbs had already put out a four-song 7" called With Illustrations in 1982 with an earlier band, the Happy Cadavers.

years.src: Wikipedia: Squirrel Bait · Wikipedia: Squirrel Bait (EP)
years.h: Peter Searcy sings, Britt Walford drums, Brian McMahan joins on guitar
years.p: [[Peter Searcy|52b1ea1e-34de-4fca-aae9-35144e885d7d]] takes over vocals, [[Britt Walford|7fde6efa-750a-49c1-abee-7767230407ff]] replaces the original drummer and [[Brian McMahan|bebfec95-35a3-4cc8-b85e-8b178d09526d]] adds a second guitar. Three songs from the 1984 demo end up on the band's records.
years.xp: This is the five-piece that made the records, minus one drummer swap: Ben Daughtrey would replace Walford before the debut came out. Walford and McMahan would go on to start [[Slint|2869c510-2679-4a3f-bf15-e5e8b49f2f28]] together.

eras.title: Hüsker Dü, Big Black, and a logo from Steve Albini
eras.text: The band opens for the bands it worships, gets pitched to Bob Mould's label, and ends up on Homestead with a debut EP.

years.src: Vice: We Talk to Squirrel Bait · Popdose: The Popdose Interview
years.h: Opening for Hüsker Dü at the Jockey Club
years.p: Across the river from Cincinnati, Squirrel Bait plays "Sun God" to a crowd of 500 to 600. It is the only known live video of the band.
years.xp:
Grubbs told Vice that the band played roughly two dozen shows in its whole life and that this was "one of the most incredible nights" of his. Kids drove in from Louisville, Lexington, Indianapolis and Columbus, and the band played the Jockey Club four times, including bills with Big Black and the Meat Puppets.

Popdose reports the ages that night: Grubbs was 17, Johnson 18, Daughtrey 19 and McMahan 16.

years.src: Wikipedia: Squirrel Bait (EP) · Popdose: The Popdose Interview
years.h: Squirrel Bait EP, eight songs on Homestead
years.p: Recorded with engineer Howie Gano at Sound on Sound in Crestwood, Kentucky, and released by Homestead after Big Black and [[Naked Raygun|85d2e30c-92fd-4c7f-a2dc-f988a70e234d]] recommended the band to the label.
years.xp:
[[Bob Mould|d7f5305a-15fc-4af4-a61b-f6f45510cc8f]] of [[Hüsker Dü|5c4c90a4-539f-4101-83cf-301bc6a94e06]] had offered to put the record out on his Reflex label after Squirrel Bait opened for Hüsker Dü, and praised the band in Spin. The band went with Homestead instead. Spin's John Leland wrote that it "doesn't just assault you. It consumes you."

Ben Daughtrey took over from Walford on drums before release. Two songs came from earlier demo sessions. Steve Albini of Big Black made the sleeve art and, per Popdose, turned a flyer he designed for a Squirrel Bait, Urge Overkill and Big Black show into the band's logo. The Shins later recreated the cover for their "New Slang" video. Grubbs and Johnson left for college in summer 1985, and Popdose has the band splitting then before re-forming.

eras.title: One last summer, then Skag Heaven
eras.text: The band regroups for a summer tour and a session, then goes back to school. Its members are already starting the bands that made Louisville famous.

years.src: Wikipedia: Skag Heaven · Wikipedia: Squirrel Bait
years.p: A single of "Kid Dynamite" and "Slake Train Coming" comes out on Homestead. Both songs were later added to Skag Heaven because the band only had eight songs for the LP.

years.h: Summer tour with Sonic Youth, the Descendents and Volcano Suns
years.p: Grubbs and Johnson come home from college for a tour with [[Sonic Youth|5cbef01b-cc35-4f52-af7b-d0df0c4f61b9]], the [[Descendents|f035837e-4117-438d-a524-cacf43500e68]] and [[Volcano Suns|4837e8d3-a13f-4670-9684-82970411f4bc]], using the dates to road-test new songs. In August the band records Skag Heaven with Howie Gano at Sound on Sound, then Grubbs and Johnson go back to school.
Britt Walford and Brian McMahan carry on together in Louisville and form Slint with David Pajo, who came from the band Maurice.

years.src: Wikipedia: Skag Heaven · Agit Reader: Past Perfect
years.h: Skag Heaven, 25 minutes 46 seconds, from five high schoolers
years.p: Homestead releases the LP, which closes on a cover of Phil Ochs's "Tape from California". "Too Close to the Fire" is the only song Searcy wrote alone.
years.xp: All five members were still in high school when the band made it, according to the Agit Reader. "Rose Island Road" is named for a winding country road that meant something to the band, per Wikipedia.

years.h: Grubbs and Johnson start Bastro in Washington, D.C.
years.p: David Grubbs and Clark Johnson form the trio Bastro with drummer John McEntire.

eras.title: The family tree
eras.text: Squirrel Bait ends for good, and its members become the reason people still ask about it.

years.p: Wikipedia dates the breakup to 1988, blaming artistic tensions and members leaving for higher education. Johnson goes into law in Louisville.

years.src: Wikipedia: Peter Searcy · Agit Reader: Past Perfect
years.p: [[Peter Searcy|52b1ea1e-34de-4fca-aae9-35144e885d7d]] plays with Big Wheel from 1989 to 1993 and releases three albums, two on Mammoth. Before that, he and Ben Daughtrey formed the funk-rock band Fanci Pantz, which drew label interest but broke up before making an album.

[[Slint|2869c510-2679-4a3f-bf15-e5e8b49f2f28]] release Tweez on Jennifer Hartman Records, recorded by Steve Albini in fall 1987, the debut from the band Walford and McMahan started after Squirrel Bait.
McMahan and Walford's second album for Touch and Go, recorded live in Chicago with producer Brian Paulson, becomes the record that fans point to when they discuss where post-rock came from.
years.xp: While Slint made it, McMahan visited Paulson in Minneapolis during the sessions for Bastro's last album, Sing the Troubled Beast, and was in a near-fatal car accident, according to Wikipedia.

years.h: Bastro turns into Gastr del Sol
years.p: Grubbs moves to Chicago for graduate school at the University of Chicago and Bastro becomes [[Gastr del Sol|8f54d90b-f322-4e5d-a0fd-bdc960f2d20f]]. The 1991 date comes from Grubbs's Wikipedia page, with [[Jim O'Rourke|172aab84-4c01-4dc0-b2ad-e723033e10ec]] joining as a partner after the first album.

years.src: Wikipedia: Squirrel Bait · Wikipedia: David Grubbs
years.p: Grubbs puts out the vinyl on Dexter's Cigar, the Drag City imprint he co-runs.
years.xp: The Homestead recordings were later gathered onto a single CD.
